title: A Function-Space Approach to the Statistical Mechanics of Learning Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2609.09589v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Deep neural networks exhibit regular macroscopic behavior despite highly nonlinear dynamics in vast parameter spaces. We develop a statistical-mechanical description of learning directly in function space, treating parameter configurations as microscopic realizations and functions with their dynamical operators as macroscopic variables. For mean-squared loss, the exact error dynamics are governed by the learning operator \(M=JJ^\ast\). Combining the dynamical Boltzmann weight of the conditional stochastic dynamics with the parameter-space density of states, whose local curvature defines a statistical operator \(B\), and integrating over local fluctuations yields   $$ \Phi_{\mathrm{fluc}}(M;B)=\frac{\sigma_\xi^2}{2}\log\det(M^{-1}+B)+\mathrm{const}. $$   At fixed spectrum, this term is rotationally stationary when \([M,B]=0\), is minimized by pairing large eigenvalues of \(M\) with small eigenvalues of \(B\), and generates a local restori

translated_title: 学习动力学的函数空间统计力学方法
translated_abstract: 深度神经网络尽管在巨大的参数空间中呈现高度非线性的动力学，却展现出规则的宏观行为。我们直接在函数空间中建立了学习的统计力学描述，将参数配置视为微观实现，将函数及其动力学算子视为宏观变量。对于均方损失，精确的误差动力学由学习算子 \(M=JJ^\ast\) 决定。将条件随机动力学的动力学玻尔兹曼权重与参数空间的态密度（其局部曲率定义了统计算子 \(B\)）相结合，并对局部涨落进行积分，得到涨落势 \(\Phi_{\mathrm{fluc}}(M;B)=\frac{\sigma_\xi^2}{2}\log\det(M^{-1}+B)+\mathrm{const}\)。在固定谱条件下，当 \([M,B]=0\) 时该项处于旋转平稳状态，通过将 \(M\) 的大特征值与 \(B\) 的小特征值配对可使该项最小化，并产生局部恢复力。
tldr: 该论文提出直接在函数空间中对学习动力学进行统计力学描述，通过学习算子 \(M=JJ^\ast\) 与由态密度局部曲率定义的统计算子 \(B\) 推导出涨落势，从而解释了深度神经网络在高度非线性参数动力学下呈现规则宏观行为的原因。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a statistical-mechanical description of learning dynamics directly in function space, deriving a fluctuation potential from the learning operator \(M=JJ^\ast\) and a statistical operator \(B\) defined by the local curvature of the density of states, thereby explaining why deep neural networks exhibit regular macroscopic behavior despite highly nonlinear parameter-space dynamics.
